units.text: ⟦0⟧16.1 Options to ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧
units.sourceHTML: 16.1 Options to sdiff

units.text: Below is a summary of all of the options that GNU ⟦0⟧ accepts. Each option has two equivalent names, one of which is a single letter preceded by ‘⟦1⟧’, and the other of which is a long name preceded by ‘⟦2⟧’. Multiple single letter options (unless they take an argument) can be combined into a single command line argument. Long named options can be abbreviated to any unique prefix of their name.
units.sourceHTML: Below is a summary of all of the options that GNU sdiff accepts. Each option has two equivalent names, one of which is a single letter preceded by ‘-’, and the other of which is a long name preceded by ‘--’. Multiple single letter options (unless they take an argument) can be combined into a single command line argument. Long named options can be abbreviated to any unique prefix of their name.

units.text: Treat all files as text and compare them line-by-line, even if they do not appear to be text. See ⟦0⟧Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Treat all files as text and compare them line-by-line, even if they do not appear to be text. See Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons.

units.text: Ignore changes in amount of white space. See ⟦0⟧Suppressing Differences in Blank and Tab Spacing⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Ignore changes in amount of white space. See Suppressing Differences in Blank and Tab Spacing.

units.text: Ignore changes that just insert or delete blank lines. See ⟦0⟧Suppressing Differences Whose Lines Are All Blank⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Ignore changes that just insert or delete blank lines. See Suppressing Differences Whose Lines Are All Blank.

units.text: Change the algorithm to perhaps find a smaller set of changes. This makes ⟦0⟧ slower (sometimes much slower). See ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧ Performance Tradeoffs⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Change the algorithm to perhaps find a smaller set of changes. This makes sdiff slower (sometimes much slower). See diff Performance Tradeoffs.

units.text: Use the compatible comparison program ⟦0⟧ to compare files instead of ⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Use the compatible comparison program program to compare files instead of diff.

units.text: Ignore changes due to tab expansion. See ⟦0⟧Suppressing Differences in Blank and Tab Spacing⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Ignore changes due to tab expansion. See Suppressing Differences in Blank and Tab Spacing.

units.text: Output a summary of usage and then exit.
units.sourceHTML: Output a summary of usage and then exit.

units.text: Ignore changes in case; consider upper- and lower-case to be the same. See ⟦0⟧Suppressing Case Differences⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Ignore changes in case; consider upper- and lower-case to be the same. See Suppressing Case Differences.

units.text: Ignore changes that just insert or delete lines that match ⟦0⟧. See ⟦1⟧Suppressing Differences Whose Lines All Match a Regular Expression⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Ignore changes that just insert or delete lines that match regexp. See Suppressing Differences Whose Lines All Match a Regular Expression.

units.text: Print only the left column of two common lines. See ⟦0⟧Controlling Side by Side Format⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Print only the left column of two common lines. See Controlling Side by Side Format.

units.text: Put merged output into ⟦0⟧. This option is required for merging.
units.sourceHTML: Put merged output into file. This option is required for merging.

units.text: Do not print common lines. See ⟦0⟧Controlling Side by Side Format⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Do not print common lines. See Controlling Side by Side Format.

units.text: Use heuristics to speed handling of large files that have numerous scattered small changes. See ⟦0⟧⟦1⟧ Performance Tradeoffs⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Use heuristics to speed handling of large files that have numerous scattered small changes. See diff Performance Tradeoffs.

units.text: Strip any trailing carriage return at the end of an input line. See ⟦0⟧Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Strip any trailing carriage return at the end of an input line. See Binary Files and Forcing Text Comparisons.

units.text: Expand tabs to spaces in the output, to preserve the alignment of tabs in the input files. See ⟦0⟧Preserving Tab Stop Alignment⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Expand tabs to spaces in the output, to preserve the alignment of tabs in the input files. See Preserving Tab Stop Alignment.

units.text: Assume that tab stops are set every ⟦0⟧ (default 8) print columns. See ⟦1⟧Preserving Tab Stop Alignment⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Assume that tab stops are set every columns (default 8) print columns. See Preserving Tab Stop Alignment.

units.text: Output version information and then exit.
units.sourceHTML: Output version information and then exit.

units.text: Output at most ⟦0⟧ (default 130) print columns per line. See ⟦1⟧Controlling Side by Side Format⟦2⟧. Note that for historical reasons, this option is ⟦3⟧ in ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ in ⟦6⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Output at most columns (default 130) print columns per line. See Controlling Side by Side Format. Note that for historical reasons, this option is -W in diff, -w in sdiff.

units.text: Ignore white space when comparing lines. See ⟦0⟧Suppressing Differences in Blank and Tab Spacing⟦1⟧. Note that for historical reasons, this option is ⟦2⟧ in ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ in ⟦5⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Ignore white space when comparing lines. See Suppressing Differences in Blank and Tab Spacing. Note that for historical reasons, this option is -w in diff, -W in sdiff.

units.text: Ignore white space at line end. See ⟦0⟧Suppressing Differences in Blank and Tab Spacing⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Ignore white space at line end. See Suppressing Differences in Blank and Tab Spacing.
